title: Mock Interview with an AI agent
description:
At this event, we will invite [Alan Ho](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alan-ho-profile/) to give a speech on how to conduct a mock interview with AI on our own. He recently built an AI mock interview system that is free and incredible. You can use this system to continually polish your interview performance.

Building an Adaptive AI Interview Coach Beyond a Chatbot
As AI makes interview preparation more accessible, the real challenge is making practice personal, realistic, and evidence-based. In this session, Alan shares how Kiwi Coach was built as a compound AI system for job seekers. The platform turns a candidate’s CV and job description into a structured interview plan, then runs an adaptive text or voice interview that can ask follow-up questions based on the user’s answers.
The talk will cover how CV parsing, JD analysis, CV-JD matching, retrieval-supported reasoning, voice interaction, and report quality checks work together to create a more useful coaching experience. Learn why the value is not just in generating questions, but in designing a workflow that connects evidence, context, feedback, and user review into one interview preparation system.

title: Waiheke - Matiatia, Owhanake & Oneroa
description:
On Saturday we will walk a loop on Waiheke Island - north. This will take us from Matiatia to Owhanake to Oneroa and beyond to Moa St for a coast to coast experience.

Sturdy footwear is recommended, as the track is often muddy and slippery in places. Rain within a few days of our walk is problematic for safety reasons. If the weather is not suitable, we will postpone and try to find a good day within the next 6 months. We have a substitute walk ready, so unless the weather is really bad, you will definitely walk this day, hopefully on Waiheke!

We will initially be following the Matiatia walk, high tide option, stunning views over the harbour, round the cliff tops, mansions and sculptures, before we rejoin the roads leading into Oneroa, and down to the beach. We will take a moment in Oneroa, another toilet stop beside the beach, take in the ambience, likely find a weather conditions suitable lunch spot, then we continue across the Island down, of course, Moa Street to Blackpool beach. We can stroll along the beach reserve, stop and look at the ship wreck at Church Bay, before taking in the island life walking the back streets up to Island Bay Gelato. From there we will take the Low Track back to the ferry, arriving well before departure time, on the hour.

Whilst it is possible to buy ferry tickets before departure, it is recommended that sailors book in advance online here... https://www.fullers.co.nz/booking/

\*\*\*THE DIRT\*\*\*
• Time: Approx. .5 hours
• Distance: 11 to 12k
• Elevation gain: 200+m
• Difficulty: moderate (AllTrails)
• Terrain: various slippery surfaces, road walking, beach walking
• Grade: for our regulars, this one will be a walk in the park, only heavy breathing when you can’t decide which flavour gelato

WALKING PROTOCOL

We need to stay together as a group when we are walking. If you are slow, move over, let the person behind you pass. Each person has a responsibility to the person both in front of them and behind to stay visibly connected.

title: OWASP New Zealand - Auckland Meetup
description:
Join us for the next **OWASP New Zealand Chapter** meetup! We are gathering the local application security community for an evening of technical talks, networking, and knowledge sharing.

* **When:** Tuesday, 14th July 2026
* **Where:** **Lightspeed Office** 2 Nuffield Street, Newmarket, Auckland 1023, New Zealand
* **Time:** 5:30 PM (Doors open for networking), 6:00 PM (Presentations begin)

We present an introductory talk about the OWASP Top 10 (2025 edition) with a new item each meeting. With the new edition OWASP Top 10, we're starting at A01:2025 Broken Access Control.

**Thanks to Our Host**
A big thank you to [Lightspeed](https://www.lightspeedhq.com/au/) for sponsoring the venue and catering and for supporting the local security community.

**Agenda**

* 6:00 PM OWASP Introduction, Top 10
* 6:30 PM Break
* 6:45 PM Technical Talk

**Technical Topic Speaker: Ricky Gummadi**
Ricky Gummadi is a Senior Solution Architect at Microsoft, based in Auckland, focused on AI, cloud architecture, and developer platforms. He works closely with enterprise customers across New Zealand to design and implement production-ready AI systems. Ricky is also part of the core development team contributing to the Agent Governance Toolkit, with a focus on enabling safe, reliable, and governed agentic AI workloads.
**Talk Title: Agentic AI Governance**
As AI systems evolve from assistants to autonomous agents, the focus shifts from what the model says to what the system actually does. This talk introduces the Agent Governance Toolkit (AGT), a framework for bringing deterministic, runtime governance to agentic systems. We’ll explore why prompt-based safety is not sufficient for production scenarios, walk through the OWASP Agentic Top 10 risks, and look at how policies, identity, sandboxing, and observability can be applied to mitigate these risks in real-world architectures.

location: MOTAT, 805 Great North Road and 98 Motions Road, Western Springs, Auckland, Auckland
description:
LIVE Days are interactive and hands-on days filled with learning, play and special moments, perfect for the whole whānau!
With live entertainment, collection items, plus plenty of activities - there's a little something for everyone.
This July at LIVE DAY: Weather Science uncover the stories of the weather-related stars in the Matariki cluster, Waipunarangi and Ururangi.
Waipunarangi is associated with the various forms of rain that we experience throughout the year as it falls from the sky and washes over the earth, nourishing all living things. If you can’t see Waipunarangi clearly during Matariki, the year will bring lots of rain and maybe some flooding. If she’s bright and clear, the rain will be light.
Ururangi connects us to the different winds and this whetū determines the nature of these winds. If Ururangi is hard to see when the cluster of Matariki rises, the year will be windy. If he is bright and clear, the winds will be calm.
Make and take home your own cloud finder, have fun with weather science experiments featuring raindrops and rainbows, and find out more about the different winds and how they work at our latest exhibition Ngā hau a Tāwhirirangi Forces of Flight, in the Aviation Hall.
Included in General Admission.
We recommend parking outside the Aviation Hall and enjoying the free heritage tram ride between sites.

title: Haerenga
location: Studio One Toi Tū, 1 Ponsonby Road, Grey Lynn, Auckland 1011, Auckland
description:
Haerenga by noa hāmana (Ngāpuhi, Ngāti Kura, Ngāti Toa) explores Māori migration and its continuation in the 21st century. Waves of dispersal across Te Moana-nui-a-Kiwa brought interludes of radical cultural adaptation, generating ancestral stories that hold mana and connect tangata Māori to whakapapa.
Migration holds a paradox of possibility and loss, raising questions of choice, push and pull – echoed today in movement from Aotearoa to Australia. Rooted in colonial economic histories, these cross-colony pathways have long carried the weight of displacement. Haerenga returns to submerged dreams and forgotten stories, revealing culture as fluid, interconnected and continually redefined.

title: He Taniwha, He Tipua
location: Studio One Toi Tū, 1 Ponsonby Road, Grey Lynn, Auckland 1011, Auckland
description:
He Taniwha, He Tipua explores narratives of taniwha in te ao Māori.
This exhibition brings together a collective of three toi Māori practitioners, Madison Redman (Ngāti Kahu ki Whangaroa, Ngāpuhi), Fern Ngatai (Ngāti Porou, Tainui) and Tristan Marler (Te Rarawa, Te Aupōuri), to express the diverse representations and symbolic significance of taniwha across Aotearoa.
Through the lens of pūrākau and toi Māori, He Taniwha, He Tipua examines the origins, guardianship roles and relationships of taniwha with different iwi, hapū and landscapes across the motu. These themes will be explored through paint, print, raranga and sculpture.

title: SaaS math with Shing
description:
Product people sit at the intersection of what gets built and what drives the business — but commercial conversations can feel like a different language. This session is designed to change that.

Shing will walk through how SaaS Product businesses are measured and valued, giving you the grounding to engage confidently in discussions about growth, efficiency, and business performance. You'll learn to read the metrics that your CEO, CFO, and investors are watching, understand what drives them, and spot when something is off. The session moves from the fundamentals through to the sharper edge of efficiency — how to tell the difference between growth that compounds and growth that costs too much, and how the decisions made in product directly shape the numbers that matter commercially.

By the end, you'll have a clearer picture of how your work connects to the business outcomes your company is chasing — and the language to talk about it with confidence.

**Meet Shing**
Paul Shingles (Shing) is a seasoned tech operator whose senior leadership experience spans operations, product strategy, sales, commercial proposition development and governance. As COO at Auror he is responsible for driving both Product and Commercial success leading to safer communities for everyone. Previously, as COO of Pushpay, he guided the business from scrappy startup through IPO to becoming one of New Zealand's handful of tech unicorns. He then joined Timely as Chief Customer Officer and later COO, driving international expansion and playing a key role in the company's sale to EverCommerce in 2021. Since then, he has focused on advising a number of New Zealand's leading CEOs, including working with the Movac portfolio.

Huge thanks to Auror for hosting and sponsoring this event!

title: AI Meets 3D, VR & XR: The State of Immersive Tech
description:
***NOTE!* I hit announce with the old title still in. Meetup's UI could use some love. This session is *not* the Jobs & AI topic, but I am planning to re-run that one soon as the waitlist was quite long.**

This session looks at how AI is transforming 3D, VR, and XR - from the way virtual worlds and assets get built, to how spaces get captured and rendered, to the experiences people step into, and the tools landing in creators' hands right now.

The focus is on demonstrating and discussing the SoTA advancements here which matter to developers, 3D artists, designers, and XR enthusiasts. Founders, product managers, and anyone curious about where spatial computing is heading will get plenty out of it too.

We'll explore-

* The current state of XR and immersive tech
* Generating 3D assets with AI - text-to-3D and image-to-3D
* NeRFs and Gaussian Splatting - capturing real spaces and turning them into explorable 3D
* AI-built environments and worlds - procedural and generative scene creation
* Workflow and pipeline shifts - what's changing for studios and solo creators alike
* The future impacts to gaming, UI's, and accessories

After these sessions we typically grab dinner nearby if you want to keep the conversation going and connect with other professionals.

title: On Becoming a Guinea Fowl (Zambia 2024)
description:
On an empty road in the middle of the night, Shula stumbles across the body of her uncle. As the funeral unfolds, the cousins unveil the buried secrets of their Zambian family in a vibrant reckoning with the lies we tell ourselves.

Every family, everywhere struggles with how to deal with sexual abuse when the perpetrator is a family member. Here we see how a Zambian family deal with social norms and funeral rituals when a family member was a serial abuser. The film takes us through the pain he caused to finding some kind of healing, The film was a winner at the Cannes Film Festival, one of only two I believe (the other was I am not a Witch" which we have seen)

The Reverse Shot reviewer wrote;

"In African countries, where guinea fowls are endemic, they are often kept as pets. The birds forage through manure and feed on ticks, maggots, and other parasites, helping to maintain an ecological balance between life and death, health, and disease. In Rungano Nyoni’s *On Becoming a Guinea Fowl*, a tale of a Zambian family of women grieving a dead relative while confronting the legacy of abuse he leaves in his wake, the metaphor isn’t hard to spot."

What’s in store these holidays?

Frosty adventures - challenges, team-building fun and quizzes to defrost your brain!
Cool excursions - movie days, ice skating and trips to some of Auckland’s favourite attractions!
Game on - sports showdowns, gymnastics and arcade games to keep you warm and active!
Cosy creativity - crafty creations, pyjama days and more!

How to get ready for all the fun? Simply pack a lunch, snacks, water, a hat and comfy clothes - and bring along a big smile for the winter adventure ahead!
Spaces are limited, so don’t miss out. Head to our website to check out your local centre’s schedule, download an enrolment form or pop in to sign up today!
